another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 7 years old. Can you help me figure out if I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

Firstly, are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, does he live with you, or do you contribute to the cost of looking after him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me. I'm his parent and I take care of him full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. It's great that Alex lives with you and you're his primary carer.

Next, could you tell me where you live? Specifically, are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I have a few follow-up questions to determine your eligibility.

Could you tell me which country you are currently living in, and are you or the other parent (if applicable) working for the UK government or the armed forces? This is important because some people living abroad may still qualify for Child Benefit under certain circumstances.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not working for the UK government or the armed forces - neither is Alex's other parent. We're just living abroad as regular residents.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more question to help determine your eligibility.

Are you or Alex's other parent employed by a company in the UK and paying UK National Insurance contributions, or were you previously living in the UK before moving abroad? If so, are you receiving any UK benefits such as a State Pension, bereavement benefits, or employment-related benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not employed by a UK company and I'm not paying UK National Insurance contributions. I'm not receiving any UK benefits like a State Pension or anything like that either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the United Kingdom. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad—such as those working for the UK government or armed forces, those employed by UK companies paying UK National Insurance contributions, or those receiving certain UK benefits—you've confirmed that none of these circumstances apply to you.

**If your circumstances change**, for example, if you return to live in the UK, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that time.

I hope this helps clarify things. If you have any other questions or your situation changes in the future, please don't hesitate to ask!
